chunks: And from him (Al-Haduth) from Isma'il ibn Mihran from Durust from Jamil who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the testimony of the deaf person in blood-money (diyah) cases. He said: 'The first statement is taken, and the second is not taken.'

key_terms.الْأَصَمِّ: The deaf person (one who cannot hear)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on the testimony of a deaf person in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the evidentiary weight of a deaf person's testimony in homicide cases. The Imam establishes that the first declaration is legally binding while the second is disregarded, reflecting the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and the reliability of the initial statement before potential hesitation or correction. This specific application highlights the nuanced approach of Shia jurisprudence in adapting general evidentiary rules to the unique communicative limitations of the deaf.
